headline: Q1 FY2027 beat on revenue, EPS and Azure growth (48%), but free cash flow margin fell to 20.2% from 33.0%.
summary: Microsoft's first quarter of FY2027 (ended 30 September 2026) is the only quarter since the FY2026 10-K, so this update re-tests Q1 against the 24 November 2026 update and keeps its statuses [4]. Revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion and non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 18% to $4.89, above the $4.72 consensus estimate [1][3]. Azure revenue grew 48% and commercial remaining performance obligation rose 73% to $677 billion [1]. Free cash flow is the weak point. Trailing twelve-month free cash flow was $60.0 billion at 30 September 2026, against $67.0 billion for FY2026, and the Q1 free cash flow margin was 20.2% against 33.0% a year earlier [2][3]. Net cash fell to $7.1 billion from $41.4 billion [3]. Statuses: T1 and T4 strengthened, T3 intact, T2 weakened. Consensus and price data are dated after the 10-K [3]. At $494.28 the reverse DCF implies 22.0% annual revenue growth for ten years and a 6.7% return against a 10.1% WACC [3]. The next test is Q2 FY2027 results in January 2027 [4].
results_commentary:
Free cash flow is the problem this quarter. The free cash flow margin was 20.2% in Q1 FY2027 against 33.0% a year earlier [3]. Trailing twelve-month free cash flow reached $60.0 billion at 30 September 2026, down from $67.0 billion in FY2026 [2][3]. The 10-Q data provided do not include a Q1 capex figure, so the filing cannot be used to split the decline between capex and operating cash flow. The filing does state that investments in cloud and datacenter infrastructure are increasing operating costs and may reduce operating margins [2]. Cash and short-term investments were $64.3 billion against $102.0 billion a year earlier, and net cash fell to $7.1 billion from $41.4 billion [3]. Shareholder returns of $10.2 billion in the quarter [1] add to the drawdown.

Gross margin also weakened, to 67.8% from 69.0%, a fall of 1.2 points [3]. Operating margin still improved to 49.8% from 48.9%, because operating expenses fell to 18.0% of revenue from 20.2% [3]. Operating income rose 21% to $45.9 billion, or 22% in constant currency [1]. GAAP EPS growth of 32% is inflated by OpenAI: the quarter carried a $207 million net gain against a $3.1 billion net loss a year earlier. Non-GAAP EPS growth of 18% is the better measure of the operating trend [1].

Demand is the strength. Revenue grew 19% to $92.3 billion from $77.7 billion [1][3]. Azure grew 48%, and Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 30% to $63.9 billion [1]. Commercial remaining performance obligation grew 73% to $677 billion, far faster than revenue [1]. Non-GAAP EPS of $4.89 beat the $4.72 estimate by 3.6%, the fourth straight beat [3]. Two metrics were redefined this quarter when segments were recast, so growth rates are not fully comparable with earlier disclosures [2]. Devices and Consumer revenue fell 3% to $15.5 billion, and Windows OEM and devices fell 22% [1]. Quarter-by-quarter, the data cover only Q1 FY2027, so the trend is one point and cannot show acceleration.

thesis_check.thesis: T1: Azure growth stays above 30% as the commercial backlog converts into revenue.
thesis_check.signpost: Azure growth at or above 30% in the Q2 FY2027 results (January 2027). Invalidation: Azure growth below 25% in any FY2027 quarter, or backlog growth falling well below revenue growth.
thesis_check.evidence: Azure revenue grew 48% in Q1 FY2027 [1], well above the 30% signpost and the 25% invalidation line. Commercial remaining performance obligation rose 73% to $677 billion against revenue growth of 19% [1][3]. The Azure metric was redefined this quarter [2], so the Q2 result is the first clean test.

thesis_check.thesis: T2: Free cash flow rebuilds as capex growth moderates.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2027 capex growth below 30% and positive free cash flow growth in the FY2027 10-K (July 2027). Invalidation: free cash flow falls again in FY2027, or capex growth stays above 50%.
thesis_check.evidence: The Q1 free cash flow margin fell to 20.2% from 33.0% [3], and trailing free cash flow of $60.0 billion at 30 September 2026 is below the $67.0 billion of FY2026 [2][3]. That is the pattern the invalidation test names, though the full-year test is the FY2027 10-K. Q1 capex is not in the data provided, so the capex growth test cannot be scored yet.

thesis_check.thesis: T3: The current price needs more growth than history or consensus supports, so returns will lag unless growth beats expectations.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2027 revenue of at least $396.0 billion, the consensus figure, in the FY2027 10-K (July 2027). Invalidation: FY2027 revenue growth of 22% or more, or a share price fall that lifts the implied return above the WACC.
thesis_check.evidence: Q1 revenue grew 19% to $92.3 billion [1]. Consensus FY2027 revenue of $396.0 billion implies 19.3% growth [3]. At $494.28 the reverse DCF still implies 22.0% annual growth for ten years and a 6.7% return against a 10.1% WACC [3]. Price and consensus are dated after the 10-K, as of 24 November 2026 [3].

thesis_check.thesis: T4: EPS estimates keep rising, which supports the earnings base behind the valuation.
thesis_check.signpost: EPS beat and further upward revisions at the Q2 FY2027 results (January 2027). Invalidation: a quarterly EPS miss, or cuts outnumbering raises in the 30-day revision count.
thesis_check.evidence: Non-GAAP EPS of $4.89 beat the $4.72 estimate by 3.6% [1][3]. FY2027 EPS consensus is $20.03, up 1.4% over 90 days, and FY2028 is $24.23, up 2.8%; 25 analysts raised and 3 cut in the last 30 days [3]. The Q1 beat was smaller than the 11.8% beat in the quarter ended 30 June 2026 [3].

risk_update: Risks that materialised: capital intensity and funding. Net cash fell to $7.1 billion and the free cash flow margin fell to 20.2% [2][3]. The 10-Q says the AI investments are made in advance of fully developed revenue streams and that customers may reduce, delay or shift AI workloads to other platforms [2]. It also says some strategic partners are significant Azure customers, so consumption from them may fall [2]. Risks that eased so far: demand signals in Q1 were strong, with Azure growth of 48% and backlog growth of 73% [1]. Unchanged: the cybersecurity incident and the $28.9 billion IRS claim described in the FY2026 10-K [4]; the Q1 10-Q data provided do not update these. New measurement risk: segment and metric redefinitions in Q1 reduce comparability with earlier periods [2]. Gross margin fell to 67.8% from 69.0%, and the filing ties infrastructure spending to lower operating margins [2][3].
outlook: The release says forward guidance will be given on the earnings call [1]. The guidance figures are not in the data provided, so none are cited here. Consensus, dated 24 November 2026, is FY2027 revenue of $396.0 billion (+19.3%) and EPS of $20.03, and FY2028 revenue of $478.0 billion and EPS of $24.23 [3]. FY2027 EPS has risen 1.4% over 90 days [3]. Watch the Q2 FY2027 report in January 2027: Azure growth at or above 30% (T1), and an EPS beat with further raises (T4) [4]. Watch the free cash flow margin and capex in the next 10-Q (T2). The FY2027 10-K in July 2027 tests revenue against $396.0 billion (T3). A trailing free cash flow decline that continues, or a Q2 Azure rate below 25%, would weaken the case.
